question: What tasks did they use to evaluate performance for male and female speakers?

evidence: In this paper, we first highlight the importance of TV and radio broadcast as a source of data for ASR, and the potential impact it can have. We then perform a statistical analysis of gender representation in a data set composed of four state-of-the-art corpora of French broadcast, widely used within the speech community. Finally we question the impact of such a representation on the systems developed on this data, through the perspective of an ASR system.

title: Gender Representation in French Broadcast Corpora and Its Impact on ASR Performance
answer_rationale: Text 1 mentions that performance for Punctual speakers and spontaneous speech was used to evaluate gender bias, noting a WER increase of 27.2% and 31.8% respectively between male and female speakers. Text 6 also describes the evaluation corpora containing prepared speech (ESTER1, ESTER2) and spontaneous speech (ETAPE, REPERE), which aligns with the evaluation tasks used.
